text: Lambda, map and filter let you transform a list without writing a loop.
We start with six numbers to work on.
A lambda is a function with no name — arguments, colon, and a single expression.
Map applies that lambda to every element, one at a time.
There's no return statement, because the expression itself is the return value.
Filter keeps only the elements where the lambda returns True.
Here that's the even numbers, since x mod two equals zero.
Filter keeps the element itself, not the True or False the lambda produced.
Both are lazy, so list forces them to actually produce their values.
Squares gives us the six squares, and evens gives us two, four and six.
And they compose — map times ten over evens, summed in a single expression.
Twenty plus forty plus sixty is a hundred and twenty.
